samples.sample_label: 0.04Nb steel aged at 723 K for 3 h

processing_steps.processing_steps_notes: Ingot prepared by induction melting in a water-cooled copper crucible; re-melted and swiftly poured into a rotating copper mold at high speed to obtain steel strips of 60×70×2.5 mm.

Aging treatment performed on a portion of the steel strips in a tubular vacuum furnace at 723 K for 3 h; 723 K was selected as the aging temperature giving better comprehensive mechanical properties for extended aging studies.

structures.overall_structure: Microstructure consists of ferrite (δ) and austenite (γ); irregular-shaped ferrite is randomly dispersed within the austenite matrix.

phases_present.morphology: irregular-shaped ferrite randomly dispersed within the austenite matrix

precipitates.distribution: nano-scale intragranular κ-carbides dispersed in austenite; more numerous than as-cast after 723 K/3 h aging
precipitates.coherency: coherent with austenite; SAED orientation relationship [100]γ//[100]κ

precipitates.distribution: submicron white NbC particles within the austenite matrix

defect_interactions.qualitative_or_quantitative_description: Nano-scale κ-carbides could be sheared by dislocations under plastic deformation.
Large-size NbC particles are impermeable and their strengthening contribution is assessed by the Ashby-Orowan equation.

measurement_conditions.specimen_geometry: gauge width 4 mm, gauge length 12 mm
measurement_conditions.other_conditions: minimum of four repetitions per steel strip

tensile_properties.stress_strain_curves: Engineering stress-strain curve of 0.04Nb steel aged 723 K/3 h (Figure 13b, black curve): yields near 900 MPa, hardens gradually and reaches roughly 29% strain.

measurement_conditions.other_conditions: Vickers hardness tester MH-5L, indentation load 200 gf, holding time 20 s

comparative_performance.comparison_metric: yield strength (0.04Nb steels exceed 0.02Nb steels by ≈71 MPa, mainly due to additional fine grain strengthening and dislocation strengthening)

characterization_methods.purpose: Phase identification of 0.04Nb steel in the 723 K/3 h aging state
characterization_methods.key_findings: Microstructure consists of ferrite and austenite; no significant change in austenite/ferrite diffraction peak intensity after 723 K/3 h aging.

characterization_methods.instrument_or_setup: Apollo 300 thermal field emission SEM with EBSD detector; EBSD step size 300 nm
characterization_methods.measurement_conditions: samples electropolished with 10 vol% perchloric acid alcohol solution at 25 V for 10 s prior to observation
characterization_methods.purpose: Microstructure characterization; ferrite content and austenite grain size analysis
characterization_methods.key_findings: Irregular-shaped ferrite randomly dispersed in austenite matrix; ferrite content of 0.04Nb steel aged 723 K/3 h is 17.2 vol%; submicron white NbC particles present.
Nb uniformly dispersed within austenite grains, with only sporadic Nb enrichment at grain boundaries; austenite chemistry of 0.04Nb steel: Mn 13.03, Al 8.37, Cr 3.97, C 1.33, Nb 0.038, Fe 64.07 wt%.

characterization_methods.technique: TEM (dark field/bright field) with SAED and EDS
characterization_methods.measurement_conditions: TEM specimens prepared by double-jet electropolishing in 10% perchloric acid + 90% alcohol at ≈30 °C and 35 V
characterization_methods.key_findings: Intragranular κ-carbides dispersed in austenite after 723 K/3 h aging, coherent with austenite ([100]γ//[100]κ); submicron white particles identified as NbC.

characterization_methods.measurement_conditions: indentation load 200 gf, holding time 20 s
characterization_methods.purpose: Measure microhardness of the steel strips
characterization_methods.key_findings: Average microhardness of 0.04Nb steel aged 723 K/3 h is 452 HV.

characterization_methods.measurement_conditions: ambient temperature; strain rate 2.5 × 10^-4 s^-1; gauge width 4 mm, gauge length 12 mm; minimum four repetitions per strip
characterization_methods.key_findings: 0.04Nb steel aged 723 K/3 h: yield strength 983 ± 13 MPa, tensile strength 1117 ± 12 MPa, total elongation 28 ± 2%.

characterization_methods.measurement_conditions: more than five SEM images per sample for ferrite content; multiple regions selected for κ-carbide size statistics
characterization_methods.purpose: Quantify ferrite content, NbC particle size/volume fraction, and κ-carbide size/content
characterization_methods.key_findings: Ferrite content of 0.04Nb steel aged 723 K/3 h measured as 17.2 vol%; NbC particle size and volume fraction increase slightly with aging temperature and Nb content; κ-carbide statistics reported in Figure 7.

computational_details.simulation_method: Analytical strengthening models (Taylor, Hall-Petch, particle shearing, Ashby-Orowan)
computational_details.validation_against_experiment: Strengthening contributions calculated to explain the higher yield strength of 0.04Nb steels relative to 0.02Nb steels.

analytical_models.equation_role: σ_a = (σ0 + σs + σg + σp + σd) * V_a
analytical_models.model_note: Values for austenite of 0.04Nb steel aged 723 K/3 h (Table 9).

analytical_models.equation_role: Dislocation strengthening in ferrite with M_F=2, α_F=0.4, G_F=76 GPa
analytical_models.model_note: Value for ferrite of 0.04Nb steel aged 723 K/3 h.

computational_details.boundary_and_initial_conditions: Temperature range 673–873 K; diffusion of Al and C in austenite for 0.02Nb and 0.04Nb steels
Kinetic energy cutoff 500 eV; Gaussian smearing 0.05 eV; U = 2.59 eV for Fe; vacuum spacing 15 Å; 6×6×6 Monkhorst-Pack k-point sampling

analytical_models.model_note: Nb doping significantly increases κ-carbide formation energy, impeding its growth and coarsening.

unmapped_findings: Measured bulk chemical composition of the 0.04Nb steel strip (Table 1, wt%): Mn 12.82, Al 9.12, Cr 2.99, C 1.40, Nb 0.039, Fe Bal. (block b0015/table_001)
Measured austenite matrix composition of the 0.04Nb steel (Table 4, wt%): Mn 13.03, Al 8.37, Cr 3.97, C 1.33, Nb 0.038, Fe 64.07. (block b0074/table_004)
As-cast 0.04Nb steel grain sizes: austenite 9 μm and ferrite 3.1 μm; the paper reports austenite grain size remains almost unchanged after aging treatment (shown for 823 K/3 h). (block b0031)

Intragranular κ-carbide statistics for 0.04Nb steels: volume fraction increases from 1.6 vol% (as-cast) to 26.7 vol% (823 K/3 h) and average size from 1.9 nm to 6.4 nm; numeric values for the 723 K/3 h state are not tabulated in the text. (block b0032)
0.04Nb steel aged at 723 K for 3 h exhibits the most favorable comprehensive mechanical properties among the studied aging states. (block b0118)

NbC particle average size and volume fraction in 0.04Nb steels increase slightly with higher aging temperature and Nb content (qualitative trend; no numeric data labels in Figure 4). (block b0025/figure_004)
